title: Walk ADR supersededBy and relatedAdrs at validate time, in the load-then-invert engine, not at ADR write time
context: The referee-guarantees docs page promises that `rcf define validate` proves every reference in every document resolves. The 0.27.0 walker's referential-integrity pass (`collectBrokenReferences`) walks the parent-id fields (prdId, tadId, reqId, usId, tacId, bsId) and the child-borne cross-links (fbs.acIds, fbs.contextRequirements, ts.acIds, cn.implementsAcIds / dependencies, eval.usId / acIds), but the two ADR schema fields declared for supersession semantics (`supersededBy`, `relatedAdrs`) are skipped. That leaves an honest gap between the docs promise and the tool: an ADR whose supersededBy names an id with no file on disk passes validate today. Two places are candidates for the check: (a) at ADR write time in `updateDocument` / `createDocument` (reject the write on an unresolved target), (b) at validate time in the load-then-invert walker (raise a brokenReference on the tree pass).
decision: Walk both fields inside `collectBrokenReferences`, reusing the existing `check` helper and the `brokenReference` error kind. Two additional call blocks appended to the existing ADR loop: one for `supersededBy` (single id), one for `relatedAdrs[i]` (each entry). Neither field is required by the ADR schema, so an absent or empty field is silent; a present target must resolve to a loaded ADR of the expected kind. This matches the pattern the walker already applies to every other cross-link (fbs.contextRequirements.adrIds is the closest sibling).
consequences: The docs-page promise holds by construction from this release. Existing WSD projects that carry stale supersession pointers will surface those failures on the next `rcf define validate` run, with the ADR file and the field named; the fix is a one-line edit or a targeted `define update` write. Choosing validate-time rather than write-time keeps the write path fast and repairable: a broken write path could refuse an operator's legitimate fix mid-repair (write-then-validate is the load-then-invert engine's contract for a reason).

alternativesConsidered.name: Reject at ADR write time in createDocument / updateDocument
alternativesConsidered.summary: Add a pre-write check that refuses a write whose supersededBy or relatedAdrs entry does not resolve.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Breaks the load-then-invert repair pattern that lets `define update` fix a broken chain from the middle. A supersession that references a not-yet-created ADR (mid-refactor) would be blocked; validate is the right seam to enforce whole-tree integrity.

alternativesConsidered.name: Add a separate `rcf define validate --adr-crosslinks` opt-in flag
alternativesConsidered.summary: Leave the default validate alone and expose an opt-in mode that checks the ADR cross-links.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The docs promise is universal, not opt-in. A flag-gated check is the same failure surface the referee page is being fixed to close.
